questions.title: Paint the ground from a terrain map?
questions.text: The mock has no ground tiles. A map says where grass and dirt are, and the game paints that through the camera. Paths can wander, there's no grid to see, and the same map worked under both cameras. The cost is a new floor painter and a Ground layer in LDtk.
questions.pick: Yes. It also means we don't need PixelLab's isometric tile tools, which the trial plan can't use.

questions.title: Buy before the isometric test?
questions.text: The ground works under either camera, and the sheets are angled art like our other props. Only the fence direction assumes isometric. Under today's camera it would need a straight-on fence, which is another purchase.
questions.pick: Buy now. The risk is one fence.

questions.title: Dummies against wizards
questions.text: The dummies stand taller than the wizards, and the teacher is bigger still. In a sword lesson, you'll stand right next to them. This is the prop scale question left open from the Art Trial.
questions.pick: Shrink props about a quarter when the isometric room is tried, and judge it there.

questions.title: The paid plan?
questions.text: Per PixelLab's help: Apprentice is $12 a month for 2,000 generations, against the 25 we have today. Unused generations don't roll over, and you can cancel with access until the period ends. It unlocks the pro tilesets, isometric tiles, path sets and building kits. This list doesn't need it, but it would let us try painted pro ground, buy several versions of a sheet and pick the best, and stop rationing.
questions.pick: Worth it, in a month when we'll make a lot of art: this kit, characters and the academy together. Your call, since it's your money.
